findings.sourceEvidence: „any Subsidiary Guarantor may make Restricted Payments to the Parent Borrower or any Subsidiary Guarantor;” (Section 7.6(a)(ii)); the Section 7.6 chapeau establishes this as an exception („except:”) to the general prohibition on Restricted Payments by the Parent Borrower or any Subsidiary.
findings.verifierReasoning: The operative provision grants a narrow, entity-scoped permission: only a „Subsidiary Guarantor” (a defined subset of subsidiaries) may make a Restricted Payment, and the recipient must be either the „Parent Borrower” or another „Subsidiary Guarantor”. The proposed IR records no entity scope at all, so it does not capture who is entitled to make the payment, i.e. that only a Subsidiary Guarantor may do so and not, for example, the Parent Borrower itself or a non-guarantor subsidiary. Moreover, the recipient limitation is represented only as an UNSUPPORTED condition; the IR itself discloses that the OR of the two recipient entity sets failed its composition rules. Because the condition is UNSUPPORTED rather than a usable structured expression, a downstream consumer would have no operational representation of the recipient restriction. A competent reviewer relying on the IR could therefore conclude that this exception permits Restricted Payments by a broader class of payors, and/or to recipients without the source-imposed restriction, which would alter the compliance analysis. The deterministic signal (distinct entity-scope terms „guarantor” and „borrower” not reflected in the IR) is confirmed by this reading of the source.
